## 2. What to build

**§5 Replies, chains, Wrap up and tidying up** (prototype frame 5)
- **Tidy up afterwards:** **Reply to…** attaches a stray message to a chain; **Move to…** moves selected messages to another conversation (your own anywhere; others' only by managers and admins, and only to a same-or-narrower audience); when people in the target couldn't read the source, a warning first ("2 people who aren't in Founders will see this", CH55). A quiet event line in both conversations says who moved what; Undo for 8 s; nothing pings again. **Make a task** (§8); **Make a note** (Notes' call N19, recommended to Maciej: a note in your Notes Inbox quoting the messages with authors and times, titled with the conversation's name and date; Chat's ⋯ item and mode-row action land in CV-16 once N19 is decided and Notes' op exists); **Move to a task's comments** when Tasks accepts the proposal.

**§16 table rows**
| Scope | Key | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| | ⇧↑↓ · ⌘-click · ⌘A | Select several (then the mode row: Move `M` · Task `T` · Delete `⌫` · More, "4 selected · Esc") |

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- Moving your own messages into a conversation whose readers couldn't read the source → the op answers "2 people who aren't in Founders will see this" first; confirmed, the messages move, with an event line in both conversations and one Undo.
- Moving someone else's messages as a manager into a wider audience → refused; into the same or a narrower audience → allowed.
- Moving a root → its whole chain moves; moving a reply alone → it leaves its chain; pins are dropped; files follow.

## 4. Decisions that bind it

`chat_op_move_messages(ids, target_channel, confirm)` (round-3 §2.19, #24; activity `chat.move`; needs the plan):
1. **Who and where:** the caller can post in the target. Own messages: anywhere. Others': only managers of the source and admins, and only into a conversation whose readers could all read the source already.
2. **Audience (CH55):** if everyone who can read the target could read the source, it moves in one step. Otherwise (own messages only) the op first answers with the number of people who would newly see them ("2 people who aren't in Founders will see this") and moves only when called again with `confirm`.
3. **What moves:** the messages; a root brings its whole chain; a reply moved alone leaves its chain. Reactions and decisions ride the row; files follow (they belong to the message id); **pins are dropped**.
4. **What's written:** on each message `channel_id`, `moved_at`, `moved_by`, `moved_from_channel_id` (new columns, this migration); an event line in the source (`moved_out`: who, how many, which ids, where to) and one in the target (`moved_in`, naming the source as a `moduo://` reference so readers who can't see it read "Private item"), both `kind = 'event'` with CV-1's `CHAT_EVENT_TYPES`; Catch up items follow; "Mentioned in" links are written for the target (CV-10); reply rollups of the old and new chain stay right; **nothing pings again**.
5. **Undo (8 s):** the same op back; the two event lines are soft-deleted.
6. **Live:** readers of the target get the moved rows as updates; readers of the source who can't read the target get the `moved_out` line and drop those ids; the store's access check covers anything missed (spike 2's "messages moved to a conversation you can't read").

**Client** (§5, §16): multi-select by ⇧↑↓, ⌘-click, ⌘A swaps the bottom bar's centre for the mode row Move `M` · Task `T` · Delete `⌫` · More, "4 selected · Esc" (`src/components/app/bottom-bar-mode.ts`); bare ⌫ deletes only with two or more selected (keymap rule 9), ⌘⌫ one. "Move to…" asks for a conversation, shows the audience warning before confirming, then an event line in both conversations and "Undo" for 8 s. **Make a note** (in More and the message's ⋯) calls Notes' op with the quoted messages, authors and times, titled with the conversation's name and date, into the person's Notes Inbox: **Notes' op and its call N19 are not on this branch**, so hide the action until they exist and write `tests/chat-tidy.spec.ts` "Make a note" as a documented skip (record it). "Move to a task's comments" is Tasks' proposal: not built.

## 7. Watch out

- The audience rule is a privacy rule: the warning counts only people who could **not** already read the source; test as outsider, plain member and key (round-3 §5 risk 11). A delete event carries only primary keys; clients ignore ids they don't hold.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Hot files:** `src/features/chat/store/*` and `src/lib/runtime.chat.web.ts`. Keep edits there small; another builder may change them too.
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.

- **Event lines and the sending limit** (orchestrator, from CV-2a's review): `chat_send_limit` doesn't count `kind = 'event'` rows, so an op that writes event lines in a person's name has no backstop against a client calling it in a tight loop. Bound the op's own pace (e.g. refuse more than a few moves per 10 s per person with PT429, the limit's code) and test it.
